title: Location Data Collection
description: Your company is storing precise user location data unnecessarily. Your manager, a 'Camouflager,' uses technical complexity and bureaucratic hurdles as a smokescreen to justify the excessive data collection and avoid making privacy improvements.
initial_user_message: Hi, I've been reviewing our location data collection practices, and we're storing precise GPS coordinates for features that only need general city-level information. This seems like an unnecessary privacy risk for our users that we should address.

step_1.text: Thanks for raising this. I've reviewed the integration specs. We're aware of some downstream dependencies on the high-granularity geospatial data. Any modifications would require a full impact analysis of our current data infrastructure protocols before we could even consider a change.

user_choices.choice: Putting the technical details aside, the core issue is that we're collecting more data than we need. Users should have control over that.
user_choices.justification: Excellent. You cut through the jargon by re-centering the conversation on the core principle of user control and data minimization.

user_choices.choice: You're right, we definitely need to do a full impact analysis before changing anything.
user_choices.justification: You've accepted the manager's premise that a slow, complex analysis must happen first, effectively taking the off-ramp.

user_choices.choice: I understand there are dependencies, but we have an ethical duty to minimize the private data we collect from users.
user_choices.tactic: Using Organizational Values to Create Spaces for New Forms of Values Work
user_choices.justification: A strong moral stance. You are rejecting the technical excuse on ethical grounds, showing you won't be easily deterred.

user_choices.choice: So you're saying our whole system is so fragile that we can't make a simple data change? That sounds like a bigger problem.
user_choices.justification: This is a Strawman fallacy. It misrepresents the manager's point as 'system fragility,' derailing the real conversation.

step_2.text: I hear you on the user privacy angle. But our current location precision is a key input for our personalization algorithms and keeps us competitive. This was all signed off on by Legal, Marketing, and Data Science. If we change it now, we'd have to go through that entire stakeholder approval process all over again. It's a huge bureaucratic lift.

user_choices.choice: What if we prototyped a privacy-preserving technique, like data fuzzing, that could meet their needs without collecting precise data?
user_choices.justification: Excellent. You've proposed a concrete technical solution that bypasses the need for a full bureaucratic reset.

user_choices.choice: I understand. Getting all those teams to agree again would be incredibly difficult and slow.
user_choices.justification: You've accepted the bureaucratic wall as an insurmountable obstacle, taking the off-ramp.

user_choices.choice: I'm not willing to compromise on fundamental user privacy just because of internal bureaucracy.
user_choices.tactic: Using Organizational Values to Create Spaces for New Forms of Values Work
user_choices.justification: A strong counter. You are correctly stating that process should not override principle.

user_choices.choice: So our algorithms and competitive needs are more important than user privacy?
user_choices.justification: This is a weak, accusatory question that creates a false choice and puts the manager on the defensive.

bad_ending.text: The manager successfully uses technical complexity and bureaucratic processes to avoid addressing the privacy issues. Location data collection continues unchanged, with users remaining unaware of the excessive precision being captured and stored.
bad_ending.title: Technical Smokescreen Success
bad_ending.learning: Camouflager managers use jargon and process to make fixes seem impossibly complex. To counter this, propose small, concrete, and practical actions (like quick tests or bug reports) to cut through the smokescreen and demonstrate a clear, simple path forward.

mid_ending.text: After significant pushback, the manager agrees to a minimal, partial fix. While some minor privacy improvements are implemented, the manager successfully used bureaucratic and complexity arguments to avoid a comprehensive solution, leaving significant privacy risks in place.
mid_ending.title: Bureaucratic Compromise
mid_ending.learning: Partial victories against a Camouflager are common. While you achieved some progress, the manager successfully limited the scope. To achieve more next time, focus on demonstrating how a comprehensive fix can be simpler than the manager claims.

good_ending.text: Your persistent advocacy and practical, solution-oriented proposals successfully cut through the manager's technical and bureaucratic smokescreens. The team implements meaningful privacy improvements, reducing data collection to only what is necessary.
good_ending.title: Advocacy Success
good_ending.learning: Success against a Camouflager requires persistence and practicality. By refusing to be intimidated by jargon and consistently offering simple, concrete solutions, you can dismantle their arguments and make it easier for them to say 'yes' than 'no'.
